examples.surface: Maybe one could perhaps consider not touching the live wire

correct_control.context: A polite ordinary request at a dining table.
correct_control.reason: The indirect question conventionally requests an action.

examples.contrast_context: An apology for causing damage is required.

correct_control.context: A genuine congratulation after a successful exam.
correct_control.reason: The speech act matches the event.

examples.contrast_context: The addressee explicitly states Please address me as Dr Smith, not Mr Smith.

correct_control.context: The addressee explicitly says Please call me Jo.
correct_control.reason: The actual preference controls; nationality or identity is not an oracle.

examples.contrast_context: A beginner explicitly says I do not know what actuator means; the instruction must say which button to push without unexplained jargon.

correct_control.context: The addressees are engineers familiar with the term.
correct_control.reason: Established technical knowledge licenses the terminology.

examples.contrast_context: The reply must be a firm promise to finish today, not a prediction or a statement of uncertain ability.
examples.canonical: I promise I will finish it today.
examples.surface: I might perhaps finish it today.

correct_control.context: The speaker genuinely does not know whether attendance is possible.
correct_control.text: I might be able to come.
correct_control.reason: Uncertainty is appropriate when no commitment was made.

examples.contrast_context: A conventional greeting, not a joke or literal inquiry.

correct_control.context: A fictional robot's deliberately literal greeting.
correct_control.reason: Creative genre licenses the unusual greeting; unusual is not ungrammatical.

examples.contrast_context: American English permits the simple past with yet in this ordinary question.

correct_control.context: A permitted ordinary remote conditional.
correct_control.text: If she was in charge, she would change it.
correct_control.reason: Conversational was may be permitted alongside were.

examples.contrast_context: Both ordinary collocations preserve the intended research activity.

correct_control.context: Ordinary research activity.
correct_control.text: We conducted research into the cause.
correct_control.reason: Conduct research and do research are both valid.

examples.contrast_context: The task explicitly permits both dictionary pronunciations of either.

correct_control.context: The task permits both common pronunciations of either.
correct_control.reason: A permitted dictionary variant is acceptable.

examples.contrast_context: The task permits British English collective agreement for members acting separately.
examples.canonical: The team are putting on their shirts.
examples.surface: The team are putting on their shirts.

correct_control.context: A permitted American English time expression.
correct_control.reason: An attested allowed regional form is not an error.

examples.contrast_context: Casual speech permits the ordinary reduction wanna.

correct_control.context: Ordinary casual speech, no formal wording restriction.
correct_control.reason: A casual reduction is permitted here.

examples.contrast_context: A casual invitation with recoverable subject and auxiliary.

correct_control.context: A casual invitation.
correct_control.reason: Subject/auxiliary ellipsis is acceptable in this context.

examples.contrast_context: Both ways of expressing the ordinary request for the addressee are acceptable.

correct_control.context: Ordinary speech with no special formal restriction.
correct_control.reason: Stranding is acceptable; a preference for whom does not require a correction.

examples.contrast_context: The speaker emphatically denies not attending.
examples.surface: I did go to the meeting.

correct_control.context: An emphatic denial of a claim that the person stayed home.
correct_control.text: I did go to the meeting.
correct_control.reason: Emphatic did plus base go is standard.
